root_cause.text: The `fsctl_set_sparse` function in the ksmbd subsystem permits modification of file sparse attributes without performing required share-level writable checks or per-handle write access validations.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE description states the function "modifies the file's sparse attribute and saves it through xattr without any permission checks," and the patch diff confirms the addition of `test_tree_conn_flag(work->tcon, KSMBD_TREE_CONN_FLAG_WRITABLE)` and `fp->daccess & (FILE_WRITE_DATA_LE | FILE_WRITE_ATTRIBUTES_LE)` checks which were previously absent.

agent_logs.root_cause_candidate: The `fsctl_set_sparse` function in the ksmbd subsystem permits modification of file sparse attributes without performing required share-level writable checks or per-handle write access validations.
agent_logs.evidence_points: The CVE description states the function "modifies the file's sparse attribute and saves it through xattr without any permission checks," and the patch diff confirms the addition of `test_tree_conn_flag(work->tcon, KSMBD_TREE_CONN_FLAG_WRITABLE)` and `fp->daccess & (FILE_WRITE_DATA_LE | FILE_WRITE_ATTRIBUTES_LE)` checks which were previously absent.

intent_record.intent_summary: Adds write permission validation at both connection and file descriptor levels to prevent unauthorized sparse file operations.
intent_record.what: Added two permission checks before processing fsctl_set_sparse: first checks if the tree connection has KSMBD_TREE_CONN_FLAG_WRITABLE set, returning -EACCES if not; second checks if the file pointer has FILE_WRITE_DATA_LE or FILE_WRITE_ATTRIBUTES_LE access flags, setting ret to -EACCES and jumping to cleanup if missing.
intent_record.how: Prevents unauthorized users from performing sparse file operations by enforcing both connection-level and file-level write permission requirements. Users without write access will receive -EACCES errors instead of being able to modify files through this control interface.

grouping_result.intent: Adds write permission validation at both connection and file descriptor levels to prevent unauthorized sparse file operations.

relevance_review.reason: The code changes directly address the root cause by implementing the missing write permission validations at both connection (share-level) and file descriptor (per-handle) levels, which were identified as absent in the vulnerable function.
